marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q029.takeaway: The marked dorsal hand territory is supplied by the radial nerve’s superficial cutaneous distribution.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q029.displayText: The area marked by the arrow is supplied by the radial nerve.
emphasis: The area marked by the arrow is supplied by the radial nerve

rationales.b: Posterior interosseous nerve is motor to extensor compartments and has no cutaneous hand territory.
rationales.c: Median nerve supplies palmar lateral digits and distal dorsal nail beds, not the marked radial dorsal area.
rationales.d: Ulnar nerve supplies the medial hand and medial one-and-a-half digits.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q030.takeaway: The arrow marks radial nerve in the cubital fossa; injury there can cause wrist drop.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q030.displayText: The marked structure is the radial nerve in the cubital fossa. A radial nerve lesion leads to wrist drop. Ape-thumb deformity is associated with median nerve lesion, while claw hand is associated with ulnar nerve lesion.
emphasis: The marked structure is the radial nerve in the cubital fossa
A radial nerve lesion leads to wrist drop
Ape-thumb deformity is associated with median nerve lesion, while claw hand is associated with ulnar nerve lesion

rationales.a: Ape-thumb deformity follows median thenar denervation.
rationales.b: Claw hand follows ulnar intrinsic denervation.
rationales.c: Claudication is exertional ischemic pain, not the defining consequence of radial nerve injury.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q031.takeaway: C5 contributes strongly to deltoid-mediated arm abduction through the axillary nerve.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q031.displayText: Inability to abduct the arm is most likely due to a C5 root lesion. Deltoid is the principal muscle for arm abduction and is supplied predominantly by C5 through the axillary nerve. The source also provides a table of upper-limb movements/muscles and root/nerve values used to localize lesions.
emphasis: Inability to abduct the arm is most likely due to a C5 root lesion

rationales.a: C4 is not the principal root for deltoid arm abduction.
rationales.c: C6 contributes to upper-limb movements but is not the dominant root value asked for here.
rationales.d: C7 more strongly contributes to elbow/wrist extension than primary shoulder abduction.
